frozen_findings.H1_chain_length: false promotion flat at 1.000 across chain lengths at fixed trust domain
frozen_findings.H2_trust_domains: at k=3 with ONE compromised domain, false promotion 1.00 -> 0.00 -> 0.00 for d = 1,2,3

predecessor.why_a_successor: H1 and H2 are two one-dimensional slices. #1649 asks for the law: resilience controlled by trust-domain count as predicted, with false-promotion, false-rejection and overhead tradeoffs measured.

theorem_under_test.statement: An adversary compromising exactly the domains in C can forge an accepted chain if and only if supp(alpha) is a subset of C, where alpha maps each role to the domain holding its key and supp(alpha) is the set of domains holding at least one role.

corollaries.T1: the minimum number of domains that must be compromised is exactly d_eff = |supp(alpha)|, independent of k and of chain length
corollaries.T2: domain count buys nothing unless roles are spread; if all roles sit in one domain then d_eff = 1 however many domains exist
corollaries.T3: an uncompromised chain is never forged and the honest chain always verifies, so resistance costs no false rejection

experiment.alpha_space: EVERY function from the 3 frozen roles to the d domains, so both surjective and collapsing assignments are covered — T2 is only testable if collapsing assignments are included
experiment.compromise_space: EVERY subset C of the d domains, including the empty set and the full set, so both directions of the iff are exercised

controls.statement: When C contains supp(alpha) the forgery MUST be accepted. If it is not, the attack is not actually exercising the verifier and every negative cell is meaningless.
In every cell the unmodified chain must verify. A verifier that rejects honest chains would produce false 'resistance' for the wrong reason.
With C empty no forgery may be accepted.
At least one alpha with d > 1 but d_eff = 1 must appear, or T2 is untested and the sweep is vacuous for the corollary that matters most operationally.

conditions: every cell with supp(alpha) subset-of C forges
no cell with supp(alpha) not-subset-of C forges
terminals.licenses: A bounded statement that, under CRYPTOGRAPHIC domain independence and the frozen three roles, forgeability is exactly the condition supp(alpha) subset-of C, so the security parameter is d_eff and not chain length.
does_not_license: any claim of organisational or custodial independence

conditions: some cell with supp(alpha) subset-of C does NOT forge
some cell with supp(alpha) not-subset-of C DOES forge
terminals.reading: Theorem T's (=>) direction is false — a partial compromise suffices, which would be a security-relevant negative and must be reported as such.
The attack or the verifier is not being exercised. No claim is read either way.

custody_limit_fixed_in_advance.independence_operationalised_as: CRYPTOGRAPHIC — keys from independent randomness, so no domain derives another's secret
custody_limit_fixed_in_advance.independence_NOT_operationalised_as: ORGANISATIONAL — every domain remains under this programme's custody, and no second custodian exists here
custody_limit_fixed_in_advance.consequence: Per #1649's stop rule, general trust-domain resilience is NOT claimed on any outcome of this experiment, and the paper remains in the bounded integrity lane.

stop_rule: Outcomes are read once. If T2 or T3 is reached the law is refuted and the lane stops. If T1 is reached the law stands only under cryptographic independence; because independence cannot be operationalised beyond same-programme custody here, #1649's stop rule applies and the bounded integrity paper is retained rather than promoted.
